Anane_2017 models a fed-batch culture of non-recombinant Escherichia coli W3110M and predicts biomass, glucose, acetate, and dissolved-oxygen profiles. It is a continuous, macro-kinetic model that represents glucose partitioning and acetate cycling, with oxygen transfer and the dissolved-oxygen probe response also included. The culture is run through batch and fed-batch phases, including exponential and constant feeding and glucose pulses. The model represents penicillin production by a glucose-fed culture in a batch-to-fed-batch fermentor, using a detailed unstructured mechanistic description. It predicts biomass, penicillin, glucose, dissolved oxygen, culture volume, temperature, heat generation and carbon dioxide, while accounting for pH and operating inputs such as aeration, agitation and feed. It combines substrate- and oxygen-dependent growth, pH and temperature effects, non-growth-associated penicillin formation and hydrolysis, material and energy balances, gas transfer, and pH and temperature control. The model describes growth, glucose use, and infliximab-biosimilar production by native and recombinant CHO-S cells. It combines first-order growth during the exponential phase with a threshold-modified Monod growth relationship, a cell-yield description of glucose consumption, and a Luedeking–Piret description of antibody formation. The authors developed it using batch cultures in shake flasks at different initial glucose concentrations and temperatures, then evaluated its product-formation description in instrumented batch and fed-batch bioreactors. The model describes a proprietary Chinese hamster ovary cell line producing the B1 antibody fusion protein in fed-batch bioreactors. It predicts time courses of viable cell density and glucose, glutamine, ammonia, lactate, and B1 concentrations using six coupled dynamic equations with nutrient-limited growth, metabolite inhibition, cell maintenance, and product formation mechanisms. The model represents the daily feed additions by simulating each interval between feeds and was calibrated with MCMC using seven 5,000-L culture runs.
